title: Board inspection of a licensed pharmacy and the pharmacy's self-inspection
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.24(1) the Board or its designee(s) may visit any pharmacy licensed by the Board at any time without prior notice and inspect the pharmacy staff, activities and records to determine compliance with laws and regulations governing the practice of pharmacy. Under 9.24(2) all costs associated with inspections of non-resident pharmacies shall be paid by the non-resident pharmacy or applicant. Under 9.24(3) a pharmacy shall provide all documents requested by the Board or its designee(s) in connection with an inspection or investigation. Under 247 CMR 9.19(21) a pharmacy shall perform a self-inspection within seven days of any renovation, expansion, relocation, or change of Manager of Record, and at least one time per year, utilizing a Board-approved inspection tool for routine compliance, sterile compounding, and non-sterile compounding, as applicable, and shall retain the completed self-inspection tool for at least two years.
exam_relevance: Tests unannounced Board inspection, the duty to produce documents, and the four events that trigger a self-inspection within seven days in addition to the annual one.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.fact: Self-inspection after a renovation, expansion, relocation or change of Manager of Record
numeric_facts.conditions: within seven days of the event

numeric_facts.value: at least one time per year

numeric_facts.fact: Retention of the completed self-inspection tool

common_confusions: The seven-day self-inspection is triggered by four named events only: renovation, expansion, relocation, or change of Manager of Record.
The Board-approved tool covers routine compliance, sterile compounding and non-sterile compounding, as applicable.
A recent annual self-inspection does not satisfy a triggered one, and neither limits the Board's unannounced inspection.
